requests.need: Add image sequences that can teach temporal relationships between ordered events.
requests.why_needed: The proposed boundary test requires ordered visual series that the current image-bank coverage report does not establish.

source_inputs.reference: temporal sequences with stable actors, objects, and locations
source_inputs.role: existing candidates to salvage before generation

constraints.requirement: Each series has an unambiguous order and preserves the entities needed to compare adjacent events.
Every frame and whole sequence have captions that distinguish event order from mere co-occurrence.

deliverables.description: Registry-addressable, quality-approved image sequences; reuse existing images first and commission Flux only for unresolved gaps.
deliverables.format: image registry records plus immutable selection manifest

acceptance_criteria: A coverage report states which temporal relations and controls are represented.
Every accepted sequence passes image usability, caption alignment, and ordering checks.
The exact selected files and registry records are frozen by hash before campaign authorization.
quality_checks: Reject ambiguous event order, broken continuity, watermarks, and unusable image quality.
Check for near-duplicate leakage across planned train and evaluation partitions.

requests.need: Turn selected grounded stories into fully captioned picture books with persistent characters and locations.
requests.why_needed: A proposed multimodal lesson requires narrative sequences whose visual identity and setting remain stable across pages.

source_inputs.role: canonical visual identity and setting specification

constraints.requirement: Recurring characters retain their registered identifying features across every page.
Recurring locations retain the registered layout and distinguishing features unless the story explicitly changes them.
Each caption describes the visible page event and preserves its place in the source narrative.

deliverables.description: Flux-generated canonical images for every character and anchor location defined by the frozen world bible, stored under training_data/02_thinking/grounded_stories/assets/ and indexed by reference_manifest.json.
deliverables.format: character and location image files plus JSON manifest and generation provenance

deliverables.description: Selected stories rendered as page-ordered, registry-addressable picture books with persistent visual references.
deliverables.format: book manifests, image files, captions, and provenance records

acceptance_criteria: The cleaned world bible is frozen by hash and its character and anchor-location inventory determines reference-pack coverage.
Every world-bible character and anchor location has an approved canonical image in the assets directory before rendering books.
The reference manifest links every canonical image to its world-bible entry, exact file hash, Flux request, and review receipt.
A reviewer can trace every page to its source story, caption, image, and visual references.
Identity, location, narrative-order, image-quality, and caption-alignment checks pass.
The exact source stories and all produced assets are frozen by hash before campaign authorization.
quality_checks: Reject pages with unexplained identity drift, location drift, narrative contradictions, watermarks, or unusable quality.
Keep preparation outputs out of evaluation partitions unless explicitly assigned before training.
